edges.effect_quant: Among 819 Dutch adults, current donors had substantially lower ferritin than ex-donors or never-donors but only a small, non-significant reduction in carotid intima-media thickness, and in the FeAST randomized trial of 1277 patients with peripheral arterial disease, iron-reduction phlebotomy did not significantly reduce death or the composite of death, myocardial infarction, and stroke (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.07).
edges.population: adult blood donors and adults undergoing serial iron-reduction phlebotomy
edges.mechanism: Lowering iron stores could theoretically reduce oxidative stress and slow atherosclerotic injury, which is the basis of the classic iron-heart hypothesis. In practice, any such benefit appears small, difficult to separate from healthy-donor bias, and not consistently reproduced in randomized studies.
edges.summary: The idea that blood donation protects against cardiovascular disease remains unsettled. Observational work shows lower ferritin in donors and occasional hints of less atherosclerosis, but randomized phlebotomy studies have not shown a clear reduction in major cardiovascular events or endothelial dysfunction.
edges.caveats: A major interpretive problem is healthy-donor selection, because donors are generally healthier than non-donors before the first unit is removed. Evidence from therapeutic phlebotomy in patients with vascular disease is informative mechanistically, but it is not identical to routine community blood donation.
